verifications.claim: Gary Woodland underwent successful surgery to remove a lesion (tumor) from his brain in September 2023.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'underwent surgery to remove part of a lesion from his brain in September 2023'; R2: 'Surgery in September 2023... removed much of the lesion'; R4: 'Woodland had brain surgery... to remove a lesion on his brain' (also called 'benign tumor')
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm surgery in September 2023 to remove (part of) a brain lesion/tumor, with success implied by recovery and symptom relief.

verifications.claim: The lesion was causing severe fear and anxiety symptoms.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'fear and anxiety that he just couldn’t escape... jolted awake... going to die'; R2: 'lesion on the part of his brain that caused unfounded fears that he was dying'; R4: 'lesion was on the part of the brain that controls Woodland's fear and anxiety'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state the lesion caused fear, anxiety, and related symptoms like nightmares and fear of dying.

verifications.claim: Part of the lesion remains to protect Gary Woodland's motor functions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'remove part of a lesion'; R4: 'had to leave some of it because otherwise Woodland would have had the possibility of losing sight... and the use of the left side of his body'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm not all lesion removed; R4 specifies to avoid losing motor function (use of left side of body).

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland returned to the PGA Tour in 2024.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'returned to the Tour months later'; R2: 'He returned in January 2024'; R4: 'returned to the PGA Tour in January of 2024'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm return to PGA Tour in (January) 2024.

verifications.claim: Surgeons at the Mayo Clinic removed the majority of Gary Woodland's brain lesion on Sept. 19, 2023.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R4: 'On Sept. 19, 2023, Woodland had brain surgery... remove most of the lesion'; R2: 'removed much of the lesion'; no source mentions Mayo Clinic
verifications.reasoning: Date and majority removal supported, but no reference mentions Mayo Clinic, making the specific attribution unsupported and inaccurate relative to cited sources.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland's brain surgery involved creating a hole in his skull.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'surgery... which involved a baseball-sized hole cut from the side of his head'; R4: 'drill a hole in his skull the size of a baseball'; R5: 'baseball-sized hole cut from the side of his head'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly describe drilling a baseball-sized hole in the skull for surgery.

verifications.claim: Gary Woodland's surgery removed the immediate neurological threat.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The fear, he said, was gone immediately after the surgery'
verifications.reasoning: Source directly states primary symptoms (fear/anxiety from lesion) resolved immediately post-surgery, supporting removal of immediate threat.

verifications.claim: Yahoo Sports notes that Gary Woodland developed PTSD, experiencing severe anxiety and fear of dying.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: PTSD 'as a result of the brain surgery'; pre-surgery symptoms 'fear and anxiety... going to die' from lesion, 'fear... gone immediately after the surgery'; PTSD symptoms post-surgery (hypervigilance, etc.)
verifications.reasoning: Yahoo (R1) notes PTSD post-surgery, but attributes fear of dying/anxiety to pre-surgery lesion (resolved by surgery), not to PTSD.

verifications.claim: The Killeen Daily Herald says Gary Woodland made his return to the PGA Tour in January 2024 at the Sony Open.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'His return in January 2024 looked fine'; no mention of Sony Open
verifications.reasoning: R2 (Killeen) confirms January 2024 return but does not mention Sony Open, making the specific detail inaccurate.

verifications.claim: ESPN reports Gary Woodland won the 2026 Houston Open, his first victory since the procedure.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5 (ESPN): 'Woodland wins Houston Open... first title since brain surgery' (article dated Mar 29, 2026)
verifications.reasoning: ESPN (R5) directly reports the 2026 Houston Open win as first since surgery.
